newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa urged to use UK privatisation expertise.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa urged to use UK privatisation expertise.

text.p: South Africa's government was on Thursay urged to utilise the expertise of financial institutions in the City of London in its process of privatising state assets.
Sir John Chalstrey, the Lord Mayor of London who is on a five-day visit to South Africa, said the City had wide experience in advising governments on privatisation.

"Institutions have provided advice...in Asia, especially Malaysia, South America, Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union," Chalstrey said, addressing a lunch organised by the South Africa Britain Trade Association.
"I gave no doubt that London could advise on packages on privatisation for South Africa which could assist in raising capital which would not be a drain on resources," he said.

The South African government has already tied-up with one British-based bank, the Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank Plc, which in August was awarded the tender to advise it on its overall restructuring of state assets.
The government late last year announced it would be embarking on a process of privatising state assets.
Earlier on Thursday it shortlisted seven international groups as candidates to take a stake of over $1 billion in state utility Telkom.

The government is offering a 20-30 percent stake in the telecommunications group to foreign firms as the first major step in a privatisation programme seen as a litmus test of its commitment to economic reform.
